statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. The cash-session selloff was followed by a material post-close NQ rebound, so current evidence no longer supports an elevated no-retracement path.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail is below the block threshold after post-close mean reversion, while rates and geopolitical conditions keep Stress extreme ahead of the September 24 U.S. release and opening cluster.
headline: Post-close NQ rebound lowers Tail to WATCH while rates and event risk keep Stress extreme
body: Nasdaq cash closed about 1.1% lower as the 10-year Treasury yield moved above 5.1%. Delayed MNQ quotes near 30,940-30,950 are only around 0.3% below prior settlement, indicating a substantial rebound from the afternoon weakness rather than persistent extreme holding. Fresh Finviz breadth remains weak but is supporting context only.

lookbackSummary: Over the preceding 24 hourly slots, Tail was low through most of the overnight and pre-open period, rose from WATCH at 14:00 UTC to elevated during the U.S. selloff, peaked at 34% at 17:00 UTC, and eased to 26% by 20:00 UTC as mean reversion appeared.
outlookSummary: Current Tail has eased to WATCH after the post-close rebound. The next concentrated conditional danger window is 12:30-15:15 UTC on September 24 around U.S. data, Beth Hammack remarks, the cash open and New Residential Sales; elevated Tail requires observed persistence or failed retracements.

forecast.analysis: After the cash selloff, delayed MNQ is around 30,940-30,950, only about 0.3% below prior settlement; that rebound argues against an active no-retracement path. Cash Nasdaq finished about 1.1% lower and the 10-year yield moved above 5.1%, so residual pressure remains.
drivers: Post-close MNQ has retraced materially from the afternoon weakness
Nasdaq cash closed about 1.1% lower
10-year Treasury yield moved above 5.1%
Fresh Finviz breadth remains weak in semiconductors and megacaps

news.title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq tumble as 10-year Treasury yield surges to 2007 high
Wall Street falls as oil prices, Treasury yields rise

forecast.analysis: If after-hours NQ continues rotating rather than re-extending lower, Tail should ease toward the watch boundary. Renewed selling that quickly erases the rebound and holds near fresh lows would invalidate that normalization.
drivers: After-hours rotation is the primary checkpoint
A fresh break that holds near lows would raise Tail

forecast.analysis: If the early overnight session remains two-way, Tail falls back into the low band while high rates and oil keep Stress elevated. A sudden headline gap would raise Stress first unless follow-through becomes persistent.
drivers: Two-way overnight trade supports lower Tail
Rates and oil remain background Stress amplifiers

forecast.analysis: Absent a fresh geopolitical or rates shock, overnight consolidation would favor low Tail. Persistent directional efficiency with shallow retracements would be the main reason to reclassify the hour.
drivers: Overnight consolidation is the base case
Shallow retracements would be the key invalidation

forecast.analysis: Low Tail persists if price continues to rotate around the post-close range. A synchronized move in NQ, yields and technology breadth would increase directional conviction.
drivers: Post-close range rotation keeps Tail contained
Cross-asset alignment would amplify a directional break

forecast.analysis: With distance from the U.S. close, immediate path risk should decay if no new one-way structure forms. Background macro and geopolitical uncertainty still keeps Stress well above normal.
drivers: Time decay lowers immediate path risk
Macro and geopolitical uncertainty sustain Stress

forecast.analysis: Asian-session consolidation would keep Tail low. A headline-driven gap alone would not be enough; persistence and failed retracements would be needed for a meaningful Tail increase.
drivers: Asian consolidation favors low Tail
A gap needs persistent follow-through to raise Tail

forecast.analysis: If Asia remains balanced, the strategy-relevant path risk stays low despite the previous U.S. selloff. Repeated extension after failed pullbacks would be the clearest warning sign.
drivers: Balanced Asian trade keeps Tail low
Repeated failed pullbacks would indicate mean-reversion stress

forecast.analysis: As European liquidity approaches, ranges can widen without becoming pathological. Tail rises only if direction becomes efficient and pullbacks repeatedly fail.
drivers: European liquidity can widen ranges
Directional efficiency plus failed pullbacks would raise Tail

forecast.analysis: European participation may increase volatility, but two-way price discovery would keep Tail low. A move that holds near a session extreme with aligned yields would raise concern.
drivers: European price discovery is the main checkpoint
Extreme holding with firm yields would raise Tail

forecast.analysis: If European trade remains rotational, Tail stays low even with weak prior-day technology breadth. Persistent NQ direction with improving cross-asset alignment would be the key change.
drivers: Rotational European trade keeps Tail contained
Cross-asset alignment would increase directional conviction

forecast.analysis: Late-European trade remains a transition hour. Tail stays low unless NQ develops sustained directional efficiency ahead of the U.S. premarket.
drivers: Late-European transition can increase noise
Sustained premarket directional efficiency would lift Tail

forecast.analysis: Approaching the U.S. premarket, Tail is still low if price remains two-way. Any renewed rates shock or geopolitical escalation would primarily raise Stress until the price path confirms persistence.
drivers: U.S. premarket approaches
Rates or geopolitical shocks raise Stress before Tail without path confirmation

forecast.analysis: Premarket liquidity and positioning can make direction cleaner. A persistent move that survives pullbacks would push Tail into watch territory; balanced trade would keep it near low.
drivers: Premarket positioning can sharpen direction
Persistent extension through pullbacks would raise Tail

forecast.analysis: The hour before the main U.S. release cluster carries higher uncertainty. Tail remains in watch territory unless NQ begins holding near an extreme with weak retracements.
drivers: U.S. release cluster is approaching
Extreme holding with weak retracements would raise Tail

forecast.analysis: At 12:30 UTC, U.S. international-transactions data are scheduled, followed by Beth Hammack opening remarks at 12:50 UTC. Tail reaches the top of watch only conditionally; the events themselves do not establish a one-way path.
drivers: 12:30 UTC U.S. International Transactions release
12:50 UTC Beth Hammack opening remarks
Observed post-event persistence is required to lift Tail further

forecast.analysis: The U.S. cash open at 13:30 UTC can convert premarket imbalance into persistent direction. Elevated Tail is conditional on opening-auction continuation, shallow retracements or repeated extension.
drivers: 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open
Opening-auction continuation is the main Tail checkpoint
Shallow retracements would confirm persistence

forecast.analysis: New Residential Sales are scheduled at 14:00 UTC while the opening move is still being tested. Tail is elevated only if the data/opening reaction sustains direction with failed pullbacks; orderly two-way trade would reduce it quickly.
drivers: 14:00 UTC New Residential Sales
Post-open price discovery remains active
Failed pullbacks would keep Tail elevated

forecast.analysis: If the first post-open hour remains directional with weak retracements, Tail stays just inside the elevated band. A meaningful counter-move and stabilization in yields would lower it toward watch.
drivers: Post-open retracement quality is decisive
Yield stabilization would reduce directional pressure

forecast.analysis: By mid-session, two-way price discovery would move Tail back to watch. Continued one-way extension with NQ pinned near an extreme would keep the risk state elevated instead.
drivers: Mid-session mean reversion is the key checkpoint
Session-extreme holding would prevent normalization

forecast.analysis: If U.S. trade broadens into rotation, Tail should continue easing within watch. A second directional leg would require renewed alignment across NQ, yields and technology breadth.
drivers: Midday rotation favors normalization
A second leg needs renewed cross-asset alignment

forecast.analysis: Late-day risk remains above baseline because another directional leg can emerge, but Tail stays in watch unless pullbacks fail and price holds near an extreme.
drivers: Late-session second-leg risk remains
Failed pullbacks are required for a larger Tail increase

forecast.analysis: If late-session trade becomes balanced, Tail returns to the low band. Persistent power-hour extension would be the main condition that prevents that normalization.
drivers: Balanced late-session trade lowers Tail
Power-hour extension would delay normalization

forecast.analysis: Into the next cash close, low Tail is the base case if no new persistent directional structure has formed. Stress can remain elevated even when price-path risk normalizes.
drivers: Absence of persistent direction supports low Tail
Stress can remain elevated without pathological path risk

forecastDetail.comment: Observed post-close rebound reduces current path risk, while high yields and the weak cash close keep the mapped state at WATCH.
Further after-hours rotation would ease Tail; a fresh low-holding extension would invalidate that normalization.
Two-way overnight trade would move Tail back to low despite elevated background Stress.
Overnight consolidation keeps Tail low unless shallow retracements begin to fail.
Range rotation remains the low-Tail case; synchronized cross-asset direction would be the main warning.
Time away from the U.S. close lowers immediate path risk if no fresh one-way structure develops.
